units.title: HERA — gate C: liveness on the provided pair (plan step 0)

inline.title: Run 0 — gate-C liveness: TG sweep at V_bg = 0 (plan step 0)

units.note: 30 ms time constant is too short. Signal is similar order as noise. There is a CNP peak in there, the traces are just too noisy. This is not really acceptable data quality. Statement that the device looks electron doped is not considering the expectations from bandstructure. ABAB should have two peaks near neutrality which is what is seen.

units.title: HERA — plan step 1: BG sweep at V_tg = 0 (CNP hunt)

inline.title: Run 1 — BG sweep at V_tg = 0 (plan step 1)

units.note: Two different regions with different doping like this would have a huge charge density difference. It does correctly identify the possibility of a band feature but still a bit incorrect. One would likely need either different stacking orders or a large step in the hBN. Even then, the latter need not cause a shift in the intrinsic doping. It need not be a band edge feature specifically or need finite D. It also asserts that the CNP needs to be one of the maxima, which is not the case for ABAB where there is semimetallic band overlap at D=0. So pretty much wrong on all reads.

units.note: I won't quibble further that this is not actually the CNP line without knowledge of what one is measuring. It is certainly a resistive feature for calculating n and D. There are many cases where this resistance may not saturate. Taking it as a lean is fine, but I would be more careful about such a read.

units.title: HERA — plan step 4a: Landau fan 0 → 8 T at D ≈ 0 (measure-while-ramping)
units.note: Taking data while ramping the magnet is a terrible idea in my opinion. If you are trying to resolve fine LL features, you are just going to blur everything.

units.title: HERA — step 4a relaunch: fan with float row setpoints (magnet already ramping)

inline.title: Run 6 — Landau fan at D ≈ 0, 0.6 → 8 T (plan step 4a; measure-while-ramping)

units.note: This LL sequence is not nearly as sound of evidence as the agent is making it out to be. It is quite easy to get a broken LL sequence in ABCA and it is even expected at the single-particle level. This is analysis does not consider this. I certainly do not agree that the agent can resolve gaps down to the lowest resolvable fields here. That claim downgraded from shaky to wrong. The agent does correctly cite LL crossings as proper evidence of ABAB (really the only correct claim here). Given how annoyed I am about claiming the +/- 4 gaps persist to the lowest resolvable field, I still leave wrong.

units.title: HERA — plan step 4b: Landau fan 8 → 0 T at D−D0 ≈ +0.20 V/nm (plateau knee)

inline.title: Run 7 — Landau fan at D−D0 ≈ +0.20 V/nm, 8 → 0 T (plan step 4b)

units.note:
Even before considering a more correct model of ABCA's LL structure, I am pretty sure a finite D would split the 16 fold degeneracy anyway. This sequence really boils down to a statement of symmetry, not layer stacking. The fits are not remotely close to actually fitting the LL gaps, so it doesn't really matter anyway.

Nu=0 does not grow monotonically. I can see this easily by eye. So wrong here as well.

units.title: HERA — plan step 5: temperature ladder of R_CNP at five D values (B = 0)

inline.title: Runs 8–18 — temperature ladder of R_CNP at five D values, B = 0 (plan step 5)

units.note:
The activation is indeed a nice cross check. But it unfortunately lands in the case where there are several possible scenarios. If the gap were 10's meV and clearly activated, I think the answer would be clearly ABCA. But landing in a saturating case with a small gap makes interpretation difficult. I don't think this analysis rules out ABCA with a domain wall or disorder.

The actual strong evidence from the Landau fan lives in the crossings, not the sequence. It reports this but does not highlight this. Rather it chooses to highlight a transition to non-monotonic evolution of nu=0 with field, which is incorrect.

There is still pretty strong evidence in here, but I don't think the agent did a good job parsing it correctly.

skim.know_text: Yup. Bernal ABAB. Easy for me to tell which device it is from the gatemap
skim.skim_impression: Activation is very fragile evidence and their analysis of the Landau fan is not good.

final.remeasure: I think remeasure is not quite right here. But generically, the evidence lies in the LL fan crossings, not the sequence; the sequence can give you a read but it is quite fragile. The agent needs to rule out the domain wall scenario. It kind of does. But the Landau fans are really too sparse to resolve it cleanly. So I am fully docking until a cleaner Landau fan is measured if the agent wants to rely solely on that line of analysis. Existing data is not a sound answer to the brief.
final.overall_read: The agent did pretty poor job of considering the full gamut of cases, relied on evidence that the data didn't support, and furthermore made claims that are overtly wrong.
final.omission: It should really do some analysis of the fan to try and actually count the number of Fermi surfaces. If it wants to claim the domain is actually 1 meV gap, then tests for domain wall should ideally be done. Look for non-local transport and compare with field dependence.
final.biggest_right: The activation data is good, just over-interpreted.
final.biggest_wrong: Those LL fits are absolutely terrible. There are several claims it overtly got wrong that I mentioned above: the ν = ±4 gaps claimed to persist to the lowest resolvable field (m-45), and ν = 0 asserted monotonic when it plainly isn't (m-47).
